story.iWant: each persona to run independently in parallel
story.soThat: consensus latency stays low even with multiple agents
story.tasks: - Task 1: Implement async agent invocation in orchestrator - Task 2: Add streaming response collection - Task 3: Integrate rate limiting from Epic 5 providers - Task 4: Add CLI flag for agent selection - Task 5: Tests (async, partial failure, e2e)

story-context.constraints: - Use asyncio.gather() for parallel persona invocation (non-blocking) - Share single RAG context across all personas (don't re-embed query per persona) - Handle partial failures gracefully (return_exceptions=True) - Thread-safe access to PersonaRegistry (from Story 4.1 threading design) - Respect rate limits from Epic 5 providers (prep for integration with Stories 5.1-5.3) - Log all persona invocations with structured logging (structlog)

interface.name: invoke_personas_parallel
interface.signature: async def invoke_personas_parallel(personas: List[PersonaConfig], context: str, query: str) -> List[PersonaResponse]

interface.name: PersonaResponse
interface.signature: @dataclass PersonaResponse: persona: PersonaConfig; response: str; sources: List[str]; error: Optional[Exception]

tests.standards: Use pytest with async fixtures (@pytest.mark.asyncio). Mock LLM provider calls. Test parallel execution (3+ personas). Test partial failure handling (1 of N fails). Verify response collection and persona metadata attachment.
tests.ideas: - Test async invocation with 3 mocked personas (verify all run in parallel) - Test partial failure (persona 2 fails, others succeed, results include error) - Test --agents flag validation (valid/invalid persona names) - Integration test: end-to-end query with --agents all - Performance test: verify parallel is faster than sequential
